answer: Rotating entry pulse: each round a verifiable random delay assigns identities a hidden join slot, and only slot-holders may act, so a whisper of one identity's timing cannot predict another. Attacker must split capital across many dormant identities and pay continuous upkeep through missed slots, while a garden of unrelated newcomers dilutes any single cluster's expected allocation. Enforcement ejects identities that miss assigned slots repeatedly, so the concrete cost is sustained per-identity fees with no guaranteed return.
